raw_response:
I farm the way I always have in Quzhou: I start from last year’s way, then I adjust a little if I think it will pay. On my 10.1 mu, wheat-maize is still my main road because that is what this place is built for, and with my well I can hold wheat steady. Cotton can still make money, but it takes more watching and more sprays, so I will not put too much land into it now that there are only 2 people at home and some labor goes off-farm. I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize and leave a smaller piece for cotton. For wheat, I will push fertilizer a bit because if wheat gets hungry in spring, yield drops fast and I cannot make that back later. Around here, if water is there, wheat is where I do not save too hard. For maize, I will follow behind wheat on the same land, use a hybrid, give enough nitrogen, and rely partly on summer rain, with one well irrigation if rain does not come right. For cotton, I will keep it on the lighter side of the farm, use improved seed, give more potash than wheat and maize because cotton needs strength for bolls, and I will spray more times because once insects get ahead, cotton becomes troublesome. I count money the whole season, but I would still rather spend a little more on fertilizer than lose yield from being short.
